# libultraship patch series for the 1080 port

These patches apply to **libultraship (LUS) commit `759b13401cd6903daa67a00a753066f791622e78`**
(<https://github.com/Kenix3/libultraship>, 2026-09-02, "Load TCC-compiled scripts in-memory to avoid
antivirus false-positives (#1266)"). They change only the Fast3D interpreter (`src/fast/`, `include/fast/`).
Why each change is needed: docs/1080_PC_PORT_PLAN.md, section 11 (graphics coverage) and section 14 (M2 prep).

Apply them in order, on top of the pinned commit:

```sh
git -C <libultraship> checkout 759b13401cd6903daa67a00a753066f791622e78
git -C <libultraship> am  "$PWD"/port/third_party/libultraship-patches/*.patch   # keeps the commits
# or, without commits:
git -C <libultraship> apply "$PWD"/port/third_party/libultraship-patches/*.patch
```

The files were made with `git format-patch --zero-commit --no-signature 759b134`. To change a patch, apply the
series in a scratch clone, edit or fix up the commit, and run `format-patch` again over the whole series.
Keep the series small and in libultraship's own style (`.clang-format`: 4 spaces, 120 columns), so that it
rebases easily when the pin moves.

## The patches

| # | file | what it does |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `0001-fast-G_LINE3D-for-F3DEX-1.x-ucode_f3dex_line3d.patch` | Adds the `ucode_f3dex_line3d` ucode id: the F3DEX table with **0xB5 decoded as G_LINE3D** (the L3DEX meaning) instead of G_QUAD. Adds `Interpreter::GfxSpLine3D(v0, v1, width)`, which draws the line as a quad between the two loaded vertices, extruded perpendicular to the line on screen. Its thickness is 1.5 + width / 2 native pixels (the gbi.h definition of `gSPLineW3D`), scaled by the vertical output ratio. Culling is off for lines. A line with an endpoint behind the eye (w <= 0) is dropped (no near clip yet). The enum value is appended, so the existing ucode ids (stored in OTR display-list resources) do not move. |
| 2 | `0002-fast-read-the-cycle-1-blender-fields-for-invisible-d.patch` | The "invisible" blender test (`A = 0, M = MEM`, a Z-only write) reads the **cycle 1** fields (bits 26 / 22) in 1-cycle mode, and the cycle 2 fields (bits 24 / 20) otherwise, as before. 1080 builds its 1-cycle render modes from one `GBL_c1` word and leaves cycle 2 at zero, so its Z-only mode 0x0C4C3078 was drawn opaque. Render modes that set both cycles to the same value, as the stock `G_RM_*` pairs do, behave exactly as before. |
| 3 | `0003-fast-deferred-colour-depth-read-back-API-for-ports.patch` | Adds a **read-back API** for game code that reads the N64 colour or depth buffer from the CPU. Requests are queued before `Run()`. `ServiceReadbacks()` fulfils them at the end of `Run()`, after the frame is drawn and before it is resolved or presented, so the game thread never touches the GPU. The results are ready at the next update: one frame of latency, the same as reading the last completed N64 framebuffer. Colour: `ReadbackRequestRgba5551(x, y, w, h, dst, bswap)` / `gfx_readback_rgba5551`. It returns a region in **native coordinates (320x240)** as RGBA5551, **big-endian when `bswap` is set** (the N64 memory order that the texture importers read back), taken from the native-aspect centre of the game view and scaled to the native size with a nearest-neighbour blit. Depth: `ReadbackRequestDepth(x, y)`, then `ReadbackGetDepth(x, y, &z)` (`gfx_readback_depth_request` / `_get`), batched into one `GetPixelDepth` call. The units are LUS's (the top 14 bits of the 24-bit depth, << 2), so the far plane / cleared value reads **0xFFFC**, the N64 Z clear value that `Sun_measureVisibility` tests for. |
| 4 | `0004-fast-texture-cache-invalidation-hooks-for-CPU-writte.patch` | Adds **texture-cache invalidation hooks**. `TextureCacheInvalidateRange(addr, size)` drops every cached texture whose texels or either palette start inside `[addr, addr + size)`, and marks both loaded tiles changed so the next draw looks them up again. The C entry points are `gfx_texture_cache_invalidate_range(addr, size)` and `gfx_texture_cache_delete(addr)` (the existing exact-address `TextureCacheDelete`). The port calls the range form from the `PORT` body of `gfx_flushTexture` (the `osWritebackDCache` site) and after each CPU texture writer: ScreenThumbMat_grab, Fader_buildTexture, Tv1Tmpl_blitFrame. |
| 5 | `0005-fast-let-a-port-register-low-address-ranges-as-real-.patch` | Adds `gfx_register_raw_address_range(start, size)`. `gfx_set_timg_handler_rdp` drops a G_SETTIMG whose resolved address is at or below 0x0FFFFFFF unless `dladdr` places it in a loaded module (such an address is usually an unresolved segment). The 1080 port's lists point at memory no module owns in that range: in a 32-bit non-PIE process the brk heap follows the executable at 0x08xxxxxx, and the 64-bit replayer (`port/gfx/fast3d/f3dreplay`) rebuilds a dump at its original addresses. Without the patch every texture and palette load from there is silently skipped (found by the golden tests, plan 19.6). Addresses in a registered range pass the check; nothing changes until a port registers one. |
| 6 | `0006-fast-F3DEX-1.x-LookAt-order-and-refresh-for-texture-.patch` | **G_TEXTURE_GEN LookAt order (GBI 1).** The F3D `G_MOVEMEM` handler stored `G_MV_LOOKATY` (0x82) in `lookat[0]` and `G_MV_LOOKATX` (0x84) in `lookat[1]`, the reverse of the F3DEX2 handler and of the vertex code, which takes S from `lookat[0]`: environment maps came out transposed (S following the normal's y). Now X -> `lookat[0]`, Y -> `lookat[1]`. A new LookAt also sets `lights_changed`, so the texgen coefficients are recomputed at the next vertex: Mat_draw re-emits the LookAt every frame in the texgen list without a `G_MW_NUMLIGHT`, and the old code kept the previous LookAt until the next one. Found by the `texgen` golden scene (run 828). |
| 7 | `0007-fast-flush-the-batch-when-G_SETPRIMDEPTH-changes-the.patch` | **G_SETPRIMDEPTH flushes.** The prim depth reaches the shader as a per-draw uniform set in `Flush()`, but `G_SETPRIMDEPTH` did not flush, so consecutive `G_ZS_PRIM` rectangles with the same render state were one draw at the **last** depth set. Sprite_display draws every billboard as a TEXRECT after its own `G_SETPRIMDEPTH`, so a far sprite followed by a near one was drawn over the geometry in front of it. The handler now flushes before storing a changed depth. Found by the `sprite` golden scene (run 828). |
| 8 | `0008-fast-flip-depth-read-back-rows-when-the-game-draws-i.patch` | **Depth read-back orientation without a game framebuffer.** `AdjustPixelDepthCoordinates` takes top-down game coordinates. A game framebuffer is drawn flipped, so its rows already run top-down, but when Fast3D draws straight into the window (`mRendersToFb` false: a port without the LUS GUI, f3dreplay, and the in-process port as configured in plan 19.7) the window's rows run bottom-up, and `GetPixelDepth` / patch 3's `gfx_readback_depth_*` read the vertically mirrored pixel. y is flipped in that case. Found by the read-back check on the `splitz` golden scene (run 828). |
| 9 | `0009-fast-clamp-1-1-TEXRECT-strips-to-the-edge-when-upscaling.patch` | **Seamless TEXRECT strips above native resolution.** Large 2D images (1080's N64 logo, the trademark screen) are drawn as many narrow TEXRECT strips, each a LoadTile of 8 columns with a wide wrap mask. The RDP samples texel corners, so a 1:1 rectangle from a whole texel never blends a neighbour. Upscaled, Fast3D's bilinear filter blended each strip's edge column with its opposite edge through GL_REPEAT: a seam every 8 pixels. When a TEXRECT maps 1:1 (`|dsdx|` / `|dtdy|` == 1.0) from a whole texel and its texel range stays inside the texture, the sampler (only) clamps on that axis. Native output is unchanged (the 18 golden scenes and the real frames are byte-identical at scale 1); scaled rects (the Fader's stretched 32x32 texture) keep the wrap, which the RDP really blends across. Found on the first real frames at `--scale 3` (plan 19.8, run 832). |
| 10 | `0010-fast-forget-the-texture-image-when-G_SETTIMG-is-reje.patch` | **A rejected G_SETTIMG forgets the previous image.** `gfx_set_timg_handler_rdp` drops a G_SETTIMG that fails `IsValidResolvedAddress` (patch 5's check) but left `texture_to_load` as it was, so the next LoadBlock / LoadTile / LoadTlut read the **previous** image's base at the new image's offsets and width: a wrong texture, and a read past the old image when the new one is larger (f3dreplay's crash on Trick Attack's after-goal overlay, run 861: rows 187..203 of the 72-wide GOAL! sprite applied to a 56-wide image's base). A rejected G_SETTIMG now clears `texture_to_load` (null address, no resource); LoadBlock / LoadTile / LoadTlut skip their load while no valid image is set, so the tile / palette keeps its previous TMEM contents and nothing is read from a stale base. The rejection and each kind of skipped load log once (`[fast3d warn]`). G_SETCIMG / G_SETZIMG are not checked and Fast3D never dereferences them (it only compares them; the port reads them back as image identifiers), so they cannot go stale this way and are unchanged. Golden scenes unchanged (run 865). |
| 11 | `0011-fast-draw-nothing-for-a-reversed-TEXRECT-FILLRECT-as.patch` | **A reversed rectangle draws nothing.** The RDP's TEXRECT / FILLRECT corners are unsigned 12-bit U10.2 fields; when the lower-right corner is above or left of the upper-left one its edge walker finds no scanline (y) or marks every span crossed (x), so nothing is drawn. 1080's snowfall (SnowFall_display, snoweffects.uso) writes each flake's corners as `(x << 2) & 0xFFF` without clamping, so a flake one pixel past the left or top edge wraps to ~1023 and the hardware drops it. Fast3D drew it as a quad from (lrx, lry) to (ulx, uly): a rectangle over the whole screen with the 8x8 flake texture repeating (a grid of dots every ~18 px, Time Attack 2012-2088; the title demo's snow too). `GfxDpTextureRectangle` and `GfxDpFillRectangle` now return when `lrx < ulx || lry < uly`. Ordered rectangles are unchanged. Found against n64ref (docs/1080_PC_PORT_PLAN.md section 23). |
| 12 | `0012-fast-clip-triangles-against-the-near-and-side-planes.patch` | **F3DEX clipping (opt-in, `gfx_set_rsp_clipping(true)`).** LUS draws with `GL_DEPTH_CLAMP` and no near clip, the NoN microcodes' behaviour. F3DEX clips: a triangle crossing the near plane (z = -w) or a side plane at the clip ratio (x, y = +-ratio * w; `G_MW_CLIP`, now read by the F3D moveword handler, default 2) is clipped in clip space (Sutherland-Hodgman over the five planes, no far plane) and drawn as a fan around the polygon's **last** vertex, the RSP's pivot (checked against the N64's RDP command stream). New vertices take position, texture coordinates and colour linearly in clip space; the fog factor is computed again from their own z / w. Rectangles are not clipped. 1080: the rider's body no longer fills the screen when the camera passes through it (title demo 258, 2677, 3140, 4870). |
| 13 | `0013-fast-optional-screen-space-linear-shade-and-fog-as-t.patch` | **Screen-space linear shade (opt-in, `GfxRenderingAPIOGL::SetAffineShading(true)` before the first shader).** The RDP steps shade colour and the fog factor linearly in screen space; GL interpolates them perspective-correctly. The shade inputs and `vFog` are declared `noperspective` (desktop GL; the vertex shader moves from GLSL 1.10 to 1.30 for the qualifier; GLES unchanged). Needs patch 12: a noperspective varying over a vertex behind the eye means nothing. 1080: near-camera snow 15-45 levels too dark (title demo 705-753). |
| 14 | `0014-fast-sample-scaled-TEXRECTs-at-the-RDP-s-texel-posit.patch` | **Scaled TEXRECT texel positions.** The RDP samples a rectangle's pixel at its corner (s = uls + x * dsdx) with texel centres on whole s; GL samples pixel centres with centres on halves. With a filtering texture a TEXRECT's coordinates are offset by 0.5 - 0.5 * step (dsdx / dtdy after the tile shift): 0 for 1:1 rectangles (patch 9's strips unchanged). 1080's Fader stretches a 32x32 mask over the screen (dsdx 0.097): it sat ~5 px right and wrapped its first column into its last (title demo 4838). |
| 15 | `0015-fast-2-cycle-blender-that-alpha-blends-in-both-cycle.patch` | **Double alpha blend.** In 2-cycle mode a render mode whose two blender cycles are both IN * IN_A + MEM * (1 - IN_A) (other_mode_l top half 0x0050) blends IN * a^2 + MEM * (1 - a^2). New shader option `ALPHA_SQUARE` squares the output alpha; `SHADER_ID_SHIFT` 17 -> 18. 1080's Fader: fades were too dark at partial coverage (title demo 4837-4842). |
| 16 | `0016-fast-optional-RDP-dither-when-reading-the-framebuffe.patch` | **Dithered read-back (opt-in, `GfxRenderingAPIOGL::SetFramebufferDither(true)`).** `ReadFramebufferToCPU` truncated to RGBA5551; the RDP writes a 16-bit image through its magic-square dither (a channel rounds up when its low 3 bits exceed the pixel's dither value), and the texture unit expands 5 -> 8 bits with the top bits replicated, so a frame fed back as a texture brightens by 255/248 a pass. 1080's 2P VS results fade samples the frame into its Fader texture every step and bleaches to white on the N64 (VS 7420-7470); with truncation the port only blurred. |
| 17 | `0017-fast-optional-persistent-colour-images-one-target-pe.patch` | **Persistent colour images (opt-in, `gfx_set_persistent_color_images(true)`).** The N64 never clears a colour image by itself: a pixel a frame leaves undrawn keeps what that framebuffer held when the game last drew into it. `Run()` cleared to black. Now each frame-sized `G_SETCIMG` address (the native width, not the Z image) has its own colour target: `G_SETCIMG` loads it into the frame (scaled if the view size changed; black on first use), and the frame is stored back into it when the address changes and at the end of `Run()`. Drawing, depth (still cleared every `Run`), read-backs and presenting are unchanged; skipped with MSAA and inside a `G_SETFB` framebuffer. 1080 double-buffers (two images): where the F3DEX clipper (patch 12) cuts ground right in front of the camera, Trick Attack showed black holes (2728-2730, 3223-3226) where the N64 shows the frame of two steps before. |
| 18 | `0018-fast-widescreen-mapping-a-rectangle-hook-and-vertex-.patch` | **Hooks for a port's enhancements (all opt-in; plan 27).** `gfx_set_widescreen(true)`: with a view wider than 4:3 (the picture centred by `AdjXForAspectRatio`), partial viewports keep their centre where the picture has it, partial scissors take the picture's edges, depth read-back coordinates follow the same mapping, and a persistent colour image (patch 17) loads into the centred 4:3 with black sides; full-width viewports / scissors still cover the view. `gfx_set_rect_hook(hook)`: every G_TEXRECT / G_TEXRECTFLIP / G_FILLRECT goes through the port's hook with its command and U10.2 corners, which it may move (beyond the native screen too) or stretch over the full view width. `gfx_set_vertex_replacements(map)`: a G_VTX whose source address is a key loads the mapped vertices (the vertex counterpart of `Run()`'s matrix replacements). The 1080 port: widescreen HUD anchoring and the Fader over the full width; high-fps frames interpolated between game steps. With none of them on, output is unchanged (goldens identical). |
| 19 | `0019-fast-include-array-and-algorithm-in-interpreter.cpp.patch` | **Build fix: `interpreter.cpp` includes `<array>` and `<algorithm>`.** It uses `std::array` (class template argument deduction) and `std::clamp` and got both only through other standard headers. GCC 13's libstdc++ (Ubuntu 24.04's `g++-mingw-w64-i686-posix`, the Windows CI job) no longer pulls them in: "class template argument deduction failed" and "'clamp' is not a member of 'std'". No behaviour change. |
| 20 | `0020-fast-OpenGL-ES-3.0-backend-fixes-USE_OPENGLES.patch` | **OpenGL ES 3.0 (plan 31, Android; `USE_OPENGLES` builds only).** The fragment shader is `highp` (float, int, **sampler2D**: the default lowp sampler gave texels one level off on Mesa, and Adreno runs mediump / lowp at half precision). Patch 13's noperspective shade / fog is emulated (the vertex shader outputs varying * w and w; the fragment shader divides the two perspective-correct values, which is the screen-linear value; the varyings are renamed `...Np` by `#define`); `GL_NV_shader_noperspective_interpolation` only with `FAST_GLES_NV_NOPERSPECTIVE=1`: on Mesa it leaves some of 1080's background triangles undrawn (black wedges, attract demo 300-1900), as desktop GL's noperspective does on llvmpipe, where the emulation draws them. `GL_DEPTH_CLAMP` through `GL_EXT_depth_clamp`, else the far plane clamps in the vertex shader (near is patch 12's clipper); LUS's `gl_Position.z *= 0.3` GLES hack is removed (it changed every depth). Mirror-clamp is `GL_MIRROR_CLAMP_TO_EDGE` only with `GL_EXT_texture_mirror_clamp_to_edge`, else mirrored repeat. `GetPixelDepth`: ES reads no depth with glReadPixels: `GL_NV_read_depth` when present, else each pixel is blitted into a DEPTH24_STENCIL8 texture and a full-screen triangle writes it as a 24-bit integer into RGBA8 (round, not + 0.5: 2^24 - 0.5 is not a float); the same values as the desktop path. No MSAA on ES (3.0 resolves only to the same size and format). Shader compile errors print their log and source. `FAST_GLES_NO_EXT=1` (or a list of `noperspective`, `depth_clamp`, `mirror_clamp`, `read_depth`) takes the fallbacks. Desktop builds: the shader text and behaviour are unchanged (goldens identical). |
| 21 | `0021-fast-on-OpenGL-ES-draw-into-the-game-framebuffer-its.patch` | **On ES, draw into the game framebuffer.** `ViewportMatchesRendererResolution` returns false for `USE_OPENGLES` (as for `__APPLE__`), so Fast3D always draws into its game framebuffer and the port presents it (`finish_view`): ES reads depth only by blitting it, and whether a window surface's depth blits depends on the driver (Mesa's llvmpipe gives 0), a DEPTH24_STENCIL8 renderbuffer's always does. In that mode `AdjustPixelDepthCoordinates` pre-flips y: the framebuffer's rows run top-down and `GetPixelDepth` flips an invertY framebuffer's rows, so the read-back read the vertically mirrored pixel. **The desktop builds that draw into the framebuffer (an internal resolution other than the window's, and macOS always) still have that bug**; `FAST_FORCE_FB` (a test define) gives desktop GL the ES behaviour. |

The patches add 750 lines and remove 40 (patch 1: +93 / -6; patch 2: +5 / -2; patch 3: +129 / -2; patch 4:
+33 / -0; patch 5: +15 / -1; patch 6: +4 / -1; patch 7: +6 / -1; patch 8: +4 / -0; patch 9: +39 / -0; patch 10: +37 / -0; patch 11: +11 / -0;
patch 12: +124 / -10; patch 13: +21 / -7; patch 14: +18 / -0; patch 15: +13 / -1; patch 16: +19 / -0;
patch 17: +85 / -0; patch 18: +92 / -9; patch 19: +2 / -0); patches 20 / 21 (OpenGL ES, plan 31): +371 / -6 and +12 / -0.

## How the port uses them

- Register the memory the lists point into with `gfx_register_raw_address_range` (patch 5): the game's heap
  / arena in process, every mapped range of the dump in `f3dreplay`.
- Call `gfx_set_target_ucode` **after** `Interpreter::Init`, which resets the ucode to F3DEX2.
- Select the ucode once with `Fast::gfx_set_target_ucode(ucode_f3dex_line3d)`, for both `RcpTask_setUcodeF3DEX`
  and F3DLP.Rej. 1080 emits no G_QUAD (section 11.1), so decoding 0xB5 as a line costs nothing.
- `SetNativeDimensions(320, 240)`, so that the read-back and depth coordinates are the game's own.
- The C entry points are declared `extern "C"` in `include/fast/interpreter.h`, a C++ header. The game is C, so
  `port/gfx/` declares them again in a small C header.
- After `Init` and the ucode, `port/gfx/fast3d/port_fast3d_n64.h` turns on the N64 behaviour of patches 12, 13 and 16
  and picks the texture filter (3-point by default); `PORT_GFX_CLIP=0`, `PORT_GFX_SHADE=persp`,
  `PORT_GFX_FILTER=linear|nearest` select the LUS behaviour instead (docs/1080_PC_PORT_PLAN.md section 25).
  It also turns on patch 17's persistent framebuffers; `PORT_GFX_CLEAR=1` clears every frame instead (plan 26).
- The results of `gfx_readback_rgba5551` are written into game memory at the end of `Run()`. Call `Run()` on
  the simulation thread (decision 5), or keep `dst` from being read while the frame renders.

## Verification

Run 824 (plan 19.6): the whole series is built and **run** in `port/gfx/fast3d/f3dreplay` (64-bit, EGL, no
SDL / ImGui) and exercised by 11 golden-image scenes (`make -C port/gfx test`), G_LINE3D (patch 1) included.
Patch 5 was made with `format-patch` like the others; patches 1-4 were not regenerated (their only
difference would be the `[PATCH n/5]` subject counter).

Run 828 (plan 19.7): patches 6-8, each found by a new golden scene, were made with `format-patch` on a scratch
clone (series 1-5 applied with `git am`); 1-5 were left as they were (same bodies). 18 scenes now run, and every
scene also goes through patch 3's read-back (colour checked pixel for pixel against the frame, a 16 x 12 depth
grid hashed).

Run 877 (plan 25): patches 12-16 were made with `format-patch --start-number 12` on a scratch clone holding 1-11;
`setup-lus.sh` on the series gives that clone's tree byte for byte. Golden scenes: fader, fader_cpu and sprite
change (patches 14 / 15), every `.rb` changes (patch 16's dither); the rest are identical.

Plan 26: patch 17 was made with `format-patch -n --start-number 17` on the same clone (1-16 unchanged);
`setup-lus.sh` on the series gives its tree byte for byte. A new golden scene, `persist` (two frame images
within one list), checks it; the other 19 scenes are identical.

What was checked (run 611):
- The series applies cleanly with `git am` to a fresh clone at 759b134. The resulting tree is identical to the
  development branch.
- `src/fast/interpreter.cpp` compiles to an object (`g++ 11.4 -std=c++20 -Wall -Wextra -c`) after each patch.
  It produces no new warnings compared with the unpatched file.
  - LUS's CMake dependencies are not installed on the build machine. The compile used the header-only
    nlohmann/json, spdlog and ImGui / SDL2 headers found locally, plus two stubs: `BS_thread_pool.hpp` (the
    types `ResourceManager.h` names) and `imconfig.h` (`ImTextureID`).
  - It also needed `-DCVAR_MSAA_VALUE` / `-DCVAR_INTERNAL_RESOLUTION`, which the game normally defines.
- `check_logic.cpp` (`g++ -std=c++20 check_logic.cpp && ./a.out`) tests copies of the new expressions. These
  copies are not linked against LUS. The checks:
  - the new invisible test over all 38 constants in gfx_renderModeWord / gfx_renderMode2Word: only
    0x0C4C3078 changes, from visible to invisible, and 2-cycle results are unchanged;
  - the G_LINE3D field decode;
  - the on-screen thickness and edge parallelism of the extruded quad, for w != 1;
  - region clipping and the big-endian store;
  - the invalidation range test.

Not verified:
- Nothing was linked or run: no SDL3, OpenGL or D3D on this machine.
- `DisplayListFactory.cpp` (patch 1 adds one `case` label) was not compiled, because tinyxml2 is missing.
- A `-m32` build: the host has no 32-bit libstdc++.
- Lines, the read-back orientation (row 0 = top) and the depth values need checking on a real backend in M2.
  See "Open items" in docs/1080_PC_PORT_PLAN.md section 14.
